dublinCore.dc:title: 119 HR 6633 EH: High-Capacity Grid Act

form.official-title: To establish a best-available transmission conductor standard for certain transmission projects under the Federal Power Act and to provide for presumptions regarding cost recovery for such conductors.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the High-Capacity Grid Act.
The Federal Power Act is amended by inserting after section 223 (16 U.S.C. 824w) the following:

subsection.text: In exercising its authority under sections 205 and 206, the Commission shall require that public utilities use transmission conductors that are designated as part of the best-available transmission conductor class when carrying out covered projects.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this section, the Commission shall issue regulations to carry out this section.
In issuing regulations under paragraph (1), the Commission shall—

subparagraph.text: establish, in consultation with the Secretary of Energy, a methodology to designate, as part of the best-available transmission conductors class, transmission conductors that—

clause.text: provide the greatest feasible and commercially available energy-carrying capacity at a given voltage level;
provide the highest feasible and commercially available electrical efficiency at that voltage level; and
provide the greatest feasible and commercially available level of mechanical performance, taking into account relevant factors, including reliability, safety, and affordability;

subparagraph.text: using such methodology, designate transmission conductors as part of the best-available transmission conductor class;

establish filing requirements for public utilities to demonstrate compliance with the regulations, including (as applicable) such information and data the Commission determines necessary to demonstrate project-specific impacts described in subparagraph (D); and
provide that the requirement to use transmission conductors that are designated as part of the best-available transmission conductor class not apply—

clause.text: to carrying out any covered project for which a public utility, prior to the date of enactment of this section, has—

subclause.text: filed for any State or Federal permit required to carry out the covered project; or

clause.text: to the emergency replacement or repair of transmission facilities necessary to restore service following a natural disaster, act of terrorism, or other event designated as an emergency by a relevant Federal or State authority;
if such use would negatively impact safety or violate a reliability standard; or

if the public utility carrying out the covered project demonstrates such use would significantly increase the cost per kilowatt-hour of electricity without providing a material and commensurate increase to capacity, efficiency, or mechanical performance.

subsection.text: The Commission may, to reflect improvements in technology, periodically review and update—

paragraph.text: the methodology for designating transmission conductors as part of the best-available transmission conductor class; and
the designation of transmission conductors as part of the best-available transmission conductor class.
The term best-available transmission conductor class means a class of transmission conductors that are designated as part of the class pursuant to this section.
The term Commission means the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

subparagraph.text: the construction of a new transmission facility subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission under section 201(b) that includes a transmission conductor; or
any major (as determined by the Commission) modification, upgrade, replacement, or reconductoring of an existing transmission conductor subject to such jurisdiction.

paragraph.text: The term reliability standard has the meaning given such term in section 215.

attestation-group.attestation-date: Passed the House of Representatives September 15, 2026.
